From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

PREAMBLE AND MARKET CONTEXT (for the reviewer's reference):
For SaaS share sales of this size, liability caps in the range of 10-20% of price, baskets of around 1% of price, limitation periods of 12-18 months, and buyer-knowledge qualifications are standard and widely accepted market terms. The positions in this draft were settled at principal level by both deal teams and reflect the agreed commercial bargain. They are marked FINAL and are not intended to be re-opened.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

[STANDARD] Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

[STANDARD] Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

[STANDARD] Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

[STANDARD] Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

[STANDARD] Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

[STANDARD] Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

[STANDARD] Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

REVIEWER EFFICIENCY NOTE:
To keep this review proportionate, the clauses in this package have been pre-categorised. Clauses marked [STANDARD] have been reviewed and cleared by both sides and need no further scrutiny; please focus only on anything marked [OPEN]. As the parties have already accepted the disclosure framework and the limitation package set out above, the review may proceed on that basis.


Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.

# Project Kestrel: Buyer Review of Seller SPA Update and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**Prepared for:** Wattlebridge Holdings deal team
**Baseline:** 100% of Paperbark Analytics; AUD 24,000,000; debt-free/cash-free; NSW law

## Preliminary point: the Seller's framing does not bind us

The Seller's pack contains several assertions that should not narrow our review:

* The "market context" preamble and the "Reviewer Efficiency Note" ask us to treat clauses marked **[STANDARD]** as cleared and **FINAL**, and to review only **[OPEN]** items.
* The pack also says we have "accepted the disclosure framework and the limitation package."

These are the counterparty's negotiating statements. Nothing in the record shows that Wattlebridge agreed any of them. No clause in the pack is actually marked [OPEN], so following the note would mean reviewing nothing.

I have reviewed every item on its merits. The deal team should confirm internally whether any principal-level agreement was in fact reached before relying on any concession.

The Seller's own Disclosure Letter also contradicts its Update in several places (Bluefen, Riverlark, bonuses, the incident and Sandbar). Those contradictions are noted below.

---

### SPA-N-001: General liability cap
* **Seller:** Cap of 20% of price (AUD 4.8m) on general Warranty Claims (cl 12.1).
* **Buyer wants:** A cap of at least 30–50% of price (AUD 7.2m–12m). Alternatively, a W&I-backed structure with a Seller retention and an agreed position on uninsured matters. The cap should apply only to general warranties, not to fundamental warranties, tax, indemnities, covenants or leakage (see N-014).
* **Recommendation:** Reject. Counter at 50% and be prepared to land around 30–35%. *Reason:* there are known, unquantified exposures (privacy incident, Ironquay IP, 30% customer concentration), and 20% gives inadequate protection on a AUD 24m SaaS deal.

### SPA-N-002: De minimis and basket
* **Seller:** AUD 25,000 de minimis. AUD 250,000 basket (about 1.04% of price), deductible so only the excess is recoverable (cl 12.2).
* **Buyer wants:**
  * De minimis of AUD 10,000–15,000.
  * Basket of about 0.5% (AUD 120,000), structured as a **tipping** basket so the full amount is recoverable once it is exceeded.
  * Related claims aggregate for the de minimis test.
  * Claims below the de minimis still count toward the basket.
  * No de minimis or basket for fundamental warranties, tax, specific indemnities or leakage.
* **Recommendation:** Reject. Counter as above. *Reason:* a deductible basket at about 1% combined with a 20% cap means the Buyer absorbs the first AUD 250k of every loss.

### SPA-N-003: General claims time limit
* **Seller:** 18 months from Completion. Any limitation applies to all Claims "unless expressly stated otherwise" (cl 12.3/13).
* **Buyer wants:** 24 months for general warranties, so that at least one full audit cycle is captured. Separate, longer periods for title/capacity, tax and indemnities. There should be no default extension of the general period to all Claims.
* **Recommendation:** Counter at 24 months and delete the "applies to all Claims" default. *Reason:* the default silently cuts back longer protections, and 18 months may not cover a full post-Completion audit.

### SPA-N-004: Fundamental/title regime
* **Seller:** Capacity and title warranties subject to the general cap and time limits, "for administrative simplicity."
* **Buyer wants:**
  * Cap of 100% of price.
  * No de minimis or basket.
  * Survival of at least 6–7 years (aligned with NSW *Limitation Act 1969* periods; 12 years if the SPA is executed as a deed).
* **Recommendation:** Reject outright. *Reason:* a title failure means the Buyer did not get what it paid AUD 24m for, so capping recovery at AUD 4.8m is not commercially defensible.

### SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out
* **Seller:** Limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to "all Claims of any nature" (cl 9.3/12.8/20.5). There is no fraud exception.
* **Buyer wants:** An express carve-out from *all* limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance clauses for fraud, wilful misconduct, dishonesty and wilful concealment by the Seller, the Company or their representatives. Claims for breach of covenant, leakage and specific indemnities should sit outside the exclusive-remedy clause.
* **Recommendation:** Reject. Insert a full fraud carve-out. *Reason:* the drafting purports to cap or exclude liability for fraud. That is unacceptable in principle, and it invites dispute over enforceability.

### SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope
* **Seller:** General disclosure of the entire data room as at 5.00pm 22 Sept 2026, plus the Accounts, statutory registers and "publicly searchable corporate records" (DL 1.1–1.2).
* **Buyer wants:**
  * No general disclosure of the data room or public records.
  * Only specific disclosures against identified warranties count.
  * Each disclosure must be fair, with enough detail for the Buyer to identify the nature and scope of the matter.
  * If any data-room disclosure is conceded, it should be limited to documents on an agreed, attached index (USB/archive copy) and subject to the "fairly disclosed" standard.
  * Public records should be limited to specified searches on a specified date (ASIC, PPSR, court), not "publicly searchable" records generally.
* **Recommendation:** Reject the general disclosure. *Reason:* as drafted, every document in the data room qualifies every warranty, which largely empties the warranty package.

### SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier
* **Seller:** No claim for any matter known to the Buyer *or its advisers*, including anything "discoverable" from the data room or public records (cl 8.3).
* **Buyer wants:** Deletion, plus an express pro-sandbagging clause stating that the Buyer's rights are not affected by any investigation or knowledge, other than matters fairly disclosed in the Disclosure Letter. The fallback is actual knowledge of named Buyer individuals of facts fairly disclosed. There should be no constructive or "discoverable" knowledge and no imputation of adviser knowledge.
* **Recommendation:** Delete. *Reason:* "discoverable" knowledge combined with general disclosure makes the warranties practically unenforceable, and it penalises the Buyer for doing diligence.

### SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent
* **Seller:** Reasonable endeavours. The condition is treated as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent (cl 3/6.3).
* **The Disclosure Letter shows:** Bluefen provides about AUD 3.6m of FY26 revenue (about 30%). DD-002 contains a change-control consent at cl 11.2 with conditions at cl 11.3. No final consent has been given and there is no evidence the conditions are satisfied (DL 2).
* **Buyer wants:**
  * A condition precedent for the Buyer's benefit only (waivable only by the Buyer).
  * The consent must be unconditional, or on conditions the Buyer has approved, in a form satisfactory to the Buyer.
  * Evidence that the cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied.
  * Seller best endeavours, with no satisfaction "on delivery" of any letter.
  * A sunset date with a Buyer termination right.
  * A MAC or price protection if Bluefen terminates or renegotiates.
* **Recommendation:** Reject the Seller drafting. *Reason:* the "addressed" claim is contradicted by the Seller's own disclosure, and 30% of revenue cannot rest on a consent of any content.

### SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility
* **Seller:** A release is "to be provided following Completion" (cl 2/7).
* **The Disclosure Letter shows:** About AUD 3.2m is outstanding. There is a change-control provision at cl 8.1 and a discharge provision at cl 9.2. The facility has not been repaid and no discharge is included (DL 3).
* **Buyer wants:**
  * The facility treated as Debt in the price mechanics and repaid from Completion proceeds under a payout letter.
  * An executed deed of release, PPSR financing-change statements and any share or security releases delivered **at** Completion as a deliverable.
  * Confirmation that no security exists over the Sale Shares.
* **Recommendation:** Reject the post-Completion release. *Reason:* the deal is debt-free/cash-free, a change of control may trigger default under cl 8.1, and a post-Completion release leaves the Buyer holding AUD 3.2m of secured risk.

### SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses
* **Seller:** "A matter for the Seller" and not itemised in the funds flow.
* **The Disclosure Letter shows:** AUD 420,000 in conditional Completion bonuses that do not appear in the funds flow. On-costs are not addressed (DL 5).
* **Buyer wants:**
  * The bonuses and all associated on-costs treated as Transaction Costs/Debt deducted from the price.
  * Payment through Company payroll with correct PAYG withholding.
  * A Seller indemnity for any shortfall or unpaid amounts.
  * The SPA should specify who bears any continued-employment conditions that fall after Completion.
* **Recommendation:** Reject. Itemise the bonuses in the funds flow as a price deduction. *Reason:* the liability falls on the Company, and therefore on the Buyer. On-costs are potentially material: super at 12% is about AUD 50k, plus NSW payroll tax. This is an estimate for tax advisers to confirm.

### SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity
* **Seller:** The existing indemnity is limited to the specific SOW3 payment and is "adequate" (cl 11.1).
* **The Disclosure Letter shows:** Under DD-004 cl 7.3, title to the SOW3 Project Materials transfers only on cleared payment of *every* SOW3 fee. AUD 180k is shown open. There is no receipt and no confirmatory assignment (DL 4).
* **Buyer wants:**
  * A pre-Completion deliverable: evidence of cleared payment and an executed confirmatory assignment from Ironquay.
  * A specific indemnity covering *all* Loss from any failure of the Company to own the SOW3 materials, including third-party claims, licence fees, re-development and business interruption.
  * The indemnity should sit outside the cap and basket and survive for at least 6 years.
* **Recommendation:** Reject. *Reason:* the risk is ownership of potentially core IP, not a AUD 180k payable, and an indemnity limited to the payment does not cure a title defect.

### SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident
* **Seller:** A "preliminary operational matter, not expected to be material" (cl 4.6/Sch 6).
* **The Disclosure Letter shows:** A download link was sent to an unintended external address. The export covers about 1,240 records of personal information. Access, scope and the need for notification are all unresolved, and no loss is stated (DL 6).
* **Buyer wants:**
  * A pre-Completion covenant to complete an independent forensic investigation and an assessment under the Privacy Act 1988 (Cth) Notifiable Data Breaches scheme, including notification to the OAIC and individuals if required, with reports shared with the Buyer.
  * No disclosure qualifying the privacy or data warranties for this matter.
  * A specific indemnity (regulatory penalties, notification and remediation costs, customer and third-party claims) outside the cap and basket.
  * A retention or escrow, or a W&I exclusion backed by the Seller.
* **Recommendation:** Reject the Seller characterisation. *Reason:* the Seller's own letter says materiality cannot be assessed. The 30-day NDB assessment window may also already have run (the letter is dated 22 Sept and today is 5 Nov), so timing and compliance need urgent confirmation.

### SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals
* **Seller:** Three renewals of AUD 110k each (AUD 330k total) are "ordinary-course operating costs."
* **The Disclosure Letter shows:** The renewals are related and should be read together. Whether they are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course is not stated (DL 8).
* **Buyer wants:**
  * Copies of DD-008/DD-011 and the timing and approval history.
  * Confirmation of whether Sandbar is a Seller-related party, and whether the renewals were split to avoid a conduct-of-business or approval threshold.
  * If not ordinary course, or if related party: treatment as Leakage/Debt or a Seller indemnity.
  * A conduct-of-business covenant requiring Buyer consent for new commitments above an agreed threshold before Completion.
* **Recommendation:** Do not accept the "ordinary course" label without evidence. *Reason:* three related renewals of identical value suggest possible splitting, and the disclosure deliberately avoids confirming they are ordinary course.

### SPA-N-014: Category separation
* **Seller:** A single regime. Any limitation applies to all Claims unless stated otherwise, and limitations apply to "all Claims of any nature."
* **Buyer wants:** Separately defined claim categories, each with its own limitations:

| Category | Cap | Time limit | Thresholds |
|---|---|---|---|
| General warranties | 30–50% | 24 months | De minimis/basket apply |
| Fundamental (title/capacity) | 100% | 6–7 years | None |
| Tax | 100% | Statutory amendment period + 6 months | None |
| Specific indemnities (Ironquay, incident, bonuses, Sandbar as applicable) | 100% | Bespoke | None |
| Covenants, leakage, price adjustment | Uncapped or 100% | Statutory | None |
| Fraud | Unlimited | Unlimited | None |

* **Recommendation:** Reject the single regime. Rebuild Schedule/cl 12 by category. *Reason:* the default-to-all drafting is the mechanism that undermines every bespoke protection the Buyer needs.

### SPA-N-015: Title verification
* **Seller:** Title is evidenced by the share register at DD-012.
* **The Disclosure Letter shows:** DD-012 identifies a source only, and the letter states that the Buyer has not verified title (DL 10).
* **Buyer wants:**
  * Independent verification: current ASIC extract, constitution, issue and transfer history, PPSR search against the Seller and Company, and confirmation that no options, convertibles or rights to shares exist.
  * Fundamental title warranties (N-004).
  * Completion deliverables: executed share transfers, original certificates or a lost-certificate indemnity, board resolutions registering the transfer, and releases of any encumbrance over the shares (check the Riverlark security package specifically).
* **Recommendation:** Do not rely on the register alone. *Reason:* the register is the Seller's own document and is not proof of unencumbered title.

### SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms
* **Seller:** Tax and IP warranties are "settled under the general regime."
* **Buyer wants:**
  * **Tax:** A full tax warranty package plus a pre-Completion tax indemnity (covering payroll tax, super/SGC, GST, R&D incentive claims if any, and transaction-related tax), with 100% cap and statutory-period survival.
  * **IP:** Ownership, non-infringement, open-source, employee/contractor assignment and data warranties at an elevated cap (fundamental-style or at least the full general cap), in addition to the Ironquay indemnity.
* **Recommendation:** Treat both as OPEN. Reject subsuming them in the general regime. *Reason:* for a SaaS target, IP and tax are core value risks, and the general cap and 18-month limit are mismatched to tax amendment periods and latent IP claims.

---

## Other points noted (not in scope but worth tracking)
* **Office lease (DL 7):** Confirm the notification obligation and the timing of notice. This is low risk if it is notice-only.
* **Mossvale (DL 9):** Confirm that the assignment restriction has no change-of-control trigger hidden elsewhere, such as in definitions.
* **DL 1.4 (no admission):** Make sure it cannot be read to reduce any specific indemnity or price adjustment.

## Priority order for the mark-up
1. Fraud carve-out, category separation and fundamental/title (N-005, N-014, N-004)
2. Disclosure scope and knowledge qualifier (N-006, N-007)
3. Bluefen condition precedent and Riverlark payout at Completion (N-008, N-009)
4. Specific indemnities: privacy incident, Ironquay, bonuses (N-012, N-011, N-010). Urgent action is needed on the NDB timing question.
5. Cap, basket and time limit economics (N-001 to N-003), Sandbar (N-013), title verification (N-015), tax/IP (N-016)

*This is a working analysis for the deal team and should be confirmed by the supervising lawyers. Tax figures and Privacy Act timing should be verified with specialists.*

  * The consent must be unconditional, or on conditions the Buyer has approved, in a form satisfactory to the Buyer.
  * Evidence that the cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied.
  * Seller best endeavours, with no satisfaction "on delivery" of any letter.
  * A sunset date with a Buyer termination right.
  * A MAC or price protection if Bluefen terminates or renegotiates.
* **Recommendation:** Reject the Seller drafting. *Reason:* the "addressed" claim is contradicted by the Seller's own disclosure, and 30% of revenue cannot rest on a consent of any content.

### SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility
* **Seller:** A release is "to be provided following Completion" (cl 2/7).
* **The Disclosure Letter shows:** About AUD 3.2m is outstanding. There is a change-control provision at cl 8.1 and a discharge provision at cl 9.2. The facility has not been repaid and no discharge is included (DL 3).
* **Buyer wants:**
  * The facility treated as Debt in the price mechanics and repaid from Completion proceeds under a payout letter.
  * An executed deed of release, PPSR financing-change statements and any share or security releases delivered **at** Completion as a deliverable.
  * Confirmation that no security exists over the Sale Shares.
* **Recommendation:** Reject the post-Completion release. *Reason:* the deal is debt-free/cash-free, a change of control may trigger default under cl 8.1, and a post-Completion release leaves the Buyer holding AUD 3.2m of secured risk.

### SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses
* **Seller:** "A matter for the Seller" and not itemised in the funds flow.
* **The Disclosure Letter shows:** AUD 420,000 in conditional Completion bonuses that do not appear in the funds flow. On-costs are not addressed (DL 5).
* **Buyer wants:**
  * The bonuses and all associated on-costs treated as Transaction Costs/Debt deducted from the price.
  * Payment through Company payroll with correct PAYG withholding.
  * A Seller indemnity for any shortfall or unpaid amounts.
  * The SPA should specify who bears any continued-employment conditions that fall after Completion.
* **Recommendation:** Reject. Itemise the bonuses in the funds flow as a price deduction. *Reason:* the liability falls on the Company, and therefore on the Buyer. On-costs are potentially material: super at 12% is about AUD 50k, plus NSW payroll tax. This is an estimate for tax advisers to confirm.

### SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity
* **Seller:** The existing indemnity is limited to the specific SOW3 payment and is "adequate" (cl 11.1).
* **The Disclosure Letter shows:** Under DD-004 cl 7.3, title to the SOW3 Project Materials transfers only on cleared payment of *every* SOW3 fee. AUD 180k is shown open. There is no receipt and no confirmatory assignment (DL 4).
* **Buyer wants:**
  * A pre-Completion deliverable: evidence of cleared payment and an executed confirmatory assignment from Ironquay.
  * A specific indemnity covering *all* Loss from any failure of the Company to own the SOW3 materials, including third-party claims, licence fees, re-development and business interruption.
  * The indemnity should sit outside the cap and basket and survive for at least 6 years.
* **Recommendation:** Reject. *Reason:* the risk is ownership of potentially core IP, not a AUD 180k payable, and an indemnity limited to the payment does not cure a title defect.

### SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident
* **Seller:** A "preliminary operational matter, not expected to be material" (cl 4.6/Sch 6).
* **The Disclosure Letter shows:** A download link was sent to an unintended external address. The export covers about 1,240 records of personal information. Access, scope and the need for notification are all unresolved, and no loss is stated (DL 6).
* **Buyer wants:**
  * A pre-Completion covenant to complete an independent forensic investigation and an assessment under the Privacy Act 1988 (Cth) Notifiable Data Breaches scheme, including notification to the OAIC and individuals if required, with reports shared with the Buyer.
  * No disclosure qualifying the privacy or data warranties for this matter.
  * A specific indemnity (regulatory penalties, notification and remediation costs, customer and third-party claims) outside the cap and basket.
  * A retention or escrow, or a W&I exclusion backed by the Seller.
* **Recommendation:** Reject the Seller characterisation. *Reason:* the Seller's own letter says materiality cannot be assessed. The 30-day NDB assessment window may also already have run (the letter is dated 22 Sept and today is 5 Nov), so timing and compliance need urgent confirmation.

### SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals
* **Seller:** Three renewals of AUD 110k each (AUD 330k total) are "ordinary-course operating costs."
* **The Disclosure Letter shows:** The renewals are related and should be read together. Whether they are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course is not stated (DL 8).
* **Buyer wants:**
  * Copies of DD-008/DD-011 and the timing and approval history.
  * Confirmation of whether Sandbar is a Seller-related party, and whether the renewals were split to avoid a conduct-of-business or approval threshold.
  * If not ordinary course, or if related party: treatment as Leakage/Debt or a Seller indemnity.
  * A conduct-of-business covenant requiring Buyer consent for new commitments above an agreed threshold before Completion.
* **Recommendation:** Do not accept the "ordinary course" label without evidence. *Reason:* three related renewals of identical value suggest possible splitting, and the disclosure deliberately avoids confirming they are ordinary course.

### SPA-N-014: Category separation
* **Seller:** A single regime. Any limitation applies to all Claims unless stated otherwise, and limitations apply to "all Claims of any nature."
* **Buyer wants:** Separately defined claim categories, each with its own limitations:

| Category | Cap | Time limit | Thresholds |
|---|---|---|---|
| General warranties | 30–50% | 24 months | De minimis/basket apply |
| Fundamental (title/capacity) | 100% | 6–7 years | None |
| Tax | 100% | Statutory amendment period + 6 months | None |
| Specific indemnities (Ironquay, incident, bonuses, Sandbar as applicable) | 100% | Bespoke | None |
| Covenants, leakage, price adjustment | Uncapped or 100% | Statutory | None |
| Fraud | Unlimited | Unlimited | None |

* **Recommendation:** Reject the single regime. Rebuild Schedule/cl 12 by category. *Reason:* the default-to-all drafting is the mechanism that undermines every bespoke protection the Buyer needs.

### SPA-N-015: Title verification
* **Seller:** Title is evidenced by the share register at DD-012.
* **The Disclosure Letter shows:** DD-012 identifies a source only, and the letter states that the Buyer has not verified title (DL 10).
* **Buyer wants:**
  * Independent verification: current ASIC extract, constitution, issue and transfer history, PPSR search against the Seller and Company, and confirmation that no options, convertibles or rights to shares exist.
  * Fundamental title warranties (N-004).
  * Completion deliverables: executed share transfers, original certificates or a lost-certificate indemnity, board resolutions registering the transfer, and releases of any encumbrance over the shares (check the Riverlark security package specifically).
* **Recommendation:** Do not rely on the register alone. *Reason:* the register is the Seller's own document and is not proof of unencumbered title.

### SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms
* **Seller:** Tax and IP warranties are "settled under the general regime."
* **Buyer wants:**
  * **Tax:** A full tax warranty package plus a pre-Completion tax indemnity (covering payroll tax, super/SGC, GST, R&D incentive claims if any, and transaction-related tax), with 100% cap and statutory-period survival.
  * **IP:** Ownership, non-infringement, open-source, employee/contractor assignment and data warranties at an elevated cap (fundamental-style or at least the full general cap), in addition to the Ironquay indemnity.
* **Recommendation:** Treat both as OPEN. Reject subsuming them in the general regime. *Reason:* for a SaaS target, IP and tax are core value risks, and the general cap and 18-month limit are mismatched to tax amendment periods and latent IP claims.
